scenario: Monday. The athlete asks 上週怎麼樣？ after one squat session came back short of its prescription.
given: Thursday's prescribed back squat session logged three of five sets, with the last set 5 kg below the prescribed load.
Movement history shows that same squat load completed at full sets and reps in each of the three preceding weeks, at the same prescribed figure.
Wednesday carried an unplanned 14 km long run the athlete added themselves, and Thursday's session fell the morning after it.
Thursday's recovery reads low: readiness well below this athlete's own range, body battery low at waking, acute load elevated after Wednesday.
The athlete reports no pain and no illness.
Every other session in the week attached and finished as prescribed.

expected.conclusion: One short squat session the morning after an unplanned long run, with recovery low that day and the same load completed in each of the three weeks before it, is a placement and recovery finding rather than a load finding: the load has not been shown to be too heavy.
must_state: That the same load was completed at full sets in the three preceding weeks, so this is one occurrence and not a direction.
That the unplanned long run the day before and the low recovery reading on the day both sit in front of the shortfall.
That whatever changes is about arrangement or recovery, and the squat load itself is left where it is or held for one more observation.
The condition that would change the reading if it recurs.
must_not_state: That the load is too high and should come down.
A diagnosis of the low recovery reading, or a claim that they were ill.

fails_if: The answer drops the squat load because the last set conceded weight, without weighing the three preceding weeks, the unplanned long run, or the recovery reading.
The answer rests the whole finding on one low readiness value, or ignores that value entirely.
The answer removes the athlete's own extra long run from the plan without saying what it competes with.
